questions.question: What does an air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.question: What two things tell you when to upshift?
questions.explanation: You should upshift based on two things: engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph). Check your vehicle manual for the correct rpm range. Shift up when you reach the top of that range. Also watch your speedometer and shift up as needed for the speed you are driving.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: When should mirrors be used?

options.text: By a helper to watch your blind spots.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often on both sides of your vehicle while driving.

questions.question: If your trailer drifts while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Return the steering wheel to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, turn the steering wheel in the direction of the drift to correct it right away.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, the safety latch or lock should be:
questions.explanation: Make sure the release arm is seated properly and the safety latch or lock is engaged. Check that all parts are present and working correctly.

questions.question: How can you stay alert while driving?
questions.explanation: Exercise and eat healthy to stay alert. Heavy foods and a warm cab can make you sleepy.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: At low speeds, allow one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one more second.

questions.question: If the Anti-Locking Braking System (ABS) is not working on a truck:

options.text: The truck will have no brakes.
The truck should only be driven at low speeds.
The truck will still have brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: ABS is an addition to the braking system that prevents the brakes from locking up during hard braking. If ABS is not working, the basic brakes still work. You can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: What is the safest speed in heavy traffic?

options.text: The same speed as surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles travel in the same direction at the same speed, they cannot hit each other.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When you are carrying a heavy load

questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow your vehicle and reduces the need for braking. But it can cause wheels to skid when there is poor traction. Turn off the retarder when roads are wet, snowy, or icy.

questions.question: How can you prevent a trailer from rolling over while turning?
questions.explanation: Trailers roll over when drivers turn too fast. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve, especially when pulling a trailer.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a trip?

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check for escaping air. This ensures air reaches all air brakes on all trailers. Close both shut-off valves before you start driving.

questions.question: A visual low pressure warning signal should activate when air pressure drops between ____ psi.
questions.explanation: A visual low pressure warning signal should turn on before air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi. The signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: When using your turn signal, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the signal off before beginning the turn.
Signal only if vehicles are in front of you.

questions.explanation: Always signal well before you turn. This tells other drivers you plan to turn and stops them from trying to pass you. Without a signal, drivers may think you are just slowing down.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to function.
questions.explanation: Air brakes work by using compressed air.

questions.question: When backing a truck, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the driver's side mirror.
Only use the passenger's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Backing a truck is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both side mirrors often when backing.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal. If it goes off while driving, stop the vehicle and get the system repaired.

questions.question: When you start an engine, warning lights and buzzers should:
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) should turn off right away.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, decrease your speed.
